absences: No final RCA approval order for TA401-13, TA535-18, TA924-2, TA201-72, or TA404-13 was located in the public pages searched; those records retain filed/proposed status.
No public Tanbreez-Nukissiorfiit contract term was found; the announced 1.65 DKK/kWh price was the 2021 standard tariff, not a fixed long-term contract price.
No executed Malmbjerg power contract or $/MWh price was found; current public documents describe a future 33-43 MW third-party tender and about $150 million of power investment.
No Greenland microreactor procurement, feasibility study, utility filing, or government nuclear-energy position was found in the mine-power sources reviewed.
The Greenland government report withholds or generalizes some mine load and cost inputs; exact project-level hourly demand and commercial tariffs remain unavailable.

cases.name: GVEA-Aurora Chena power purchase agreement amendment
cases.capacity: 150,000 MWh required by December 31, 2026; estimated additional 5,000-10,000 MWh annually beginning in 2027
cases.price: $115.23/MWh base rate for 2026, up from $94.23/MWh; 2.8% annual escalation for the remaining term
cases.summary: GVEA filed an amendment to its existing Aurora Energy wholesale PPA and asked the RCA for approval by February 23, 2026, with a March 1 effective date. The proposed amendment pays $115.23/MWh in 2026, escalates 2.8% annually, and supports repairs intended to restore 150,000 MWh of annual output. The public notice does not establish that the Commission approved the amendment, so the economics remain proposed rather than final.
cases.microreactor_read: A firm 1-20 MW reactor serving Interior Alaska must compete with a filed dispatchable-power benchmark of $115.23/MWh plus 2.8% annual escalation, while matching the PPA's dependable annual volume.

cases.name: MEA-Energy 49 Houston solar power purchase agreement
cases.capacity: 6 MW solar; MEA commits to purchase 100% of metered output
cases.price: $0.06700/kWh in year one, with 1.5% annual inflation increase
cases.summary: MEA filed a 25-year PPA for all output from Energy 49's 6 MW Houston solar project. The initial price is $67/MWh with 1.5% annual escalation; delivery was required within three years of execution. The agreement also splits REC economic benefits equally and allows termination after an uncured material breach. The fetched notice requests approval and warns the Commission may vary the rate, so this record does not claim final approval.
cases.microreactor_read: This is an exact Alaska unit-size comparator: a 6 MW project secured a 25-year utility offtake at $67/MWh initially. A reactor offer must price firm output and nuclear risk against that escalator and term, not against retail tariffs.

cases.name: Tanbreez-Nukissiorfiit mine hydropower agreement
cases.capacity: up to 7.5 MW and approximately 30 GWh/year of hydropower
cases.price: standard electricity tariff, 1.65 DKK/kWh when announced in May 2021; Tanbreez funds the connection and required infrastructure
cases.summary: Tanbreez and Greenland's government-owned utility signed a cooperation agreement for mine power. Nukissiorfiit can supply about 30 GWh/year with maximum demand of 7.5 MW; Tanbreez must fund the interconnection and infrastructure and retain backup generation. The parties contemplated a later agreement and government-approved hydropower expansion if mine production exceeds available utility supply. A 2025 SEC-filed technical report still says Nukissiorfiit will supply all project power needs, but does not restate the tariff or volume.
cases.microreactor_read: This is a near-perfect 1-20 MW mine comparator: 7.5 MW firm demand bought from a public utility at 1.65 DKK/kWh, with interconnection and backup shifted to the mine. A reactor contract must allocate those same infrastructure and outage risks explicitly.

cases.name: Alaska Power Company Rate Group 5 small-facility purchase rates
cases.price: proposed SFPPRs: Allakaket/Alatna $0.5119/kWh; Bettles/Evansville $0.4413; Chistochina/Mentasta/Slana $0.0225; Eagle/Eagle Village $0.3241; Healy Lake $0.4307; Northway/Northway Village $0.2382
cases.summary: Alaska Power Company filed its first Small Facility Power Purchase Rate methodology for six Rate Group 5 load-center groupings, requesting a February 13, 2026 effective date. Proposed avoided-cost purchase rates span $22.50/MWh to $511.90/MWh, a 22.8-fold spread inside one utility tariff. The filing notice states that the RCA may approve a different rate, so these are proposed rather than final prices.
cases.microreactor_read: Village economics cannot be modeled from one statewide Alaska price. These six proposed avoided-cost rates create location-specific ceilings: a seller faces only $22.50/MWh in one grouping but more than $400/MWh in three others.

cases.name: TDX Manley 2026 COPA and small-facility purchase-rate update

parties.host: Manley Hot Springs customers and small facilities

cases.price: proposed COPA surcharge $0.8157/kWh; proposed SFPPR $1.1802/kWh; FY2026 PCE maximum $0.7424/kWh

filings.type: quarterly COPA, PCE and small facility power purchase tariff

cases.summary: TDX Manley filed a quarterly update for the period beginning September 1, 2026. It proposed raising the COPA surcharge from $0.2961 to $0.8157/kWh and the small-facility purchase rate from $0.5161 to $1.1802/kWh, while the PCE level stayed at the FY2026 statutory maximum of $0.7424/kWh. TDX also removed solar-generation kWh from its SFPPR calculation. The notice does not establish final RCA approval.
cases.microreactor_read: At Manley, the proposed $1,180.20/MWh small-facility purchase rate is an extreme remote-system value signal, but PCE and quarterly fuel-cost mechanics mean retail savings cannot be equated directly with a bankable reactor PPA.

cases.summary: GVEA filed a quarterly rate update for the period beginning June 1, 2026. The utility proposed a COPA surcharge of $0.20652/kWh, up from $0.12779, while its small-facility purchase rate fell from $0.13527 to $0.13323/kWh. The statutory notice period ended July 13, 2026, but the fetched notice does not establish the final approved rate.

regions.power_system: Greenland's government commissioned Ramboll to model isolated mine microgrids across four regions. The analysis assumes 20-year projects, an 8% discount rate, two years of construction, and constant mine operation; it models a 33 MW East load and 10 MW representative loads in South, West, and North. A May 2026 Greenland investment catalogue separately identifies a $150 million, 33-43 MW third-party power opportunity at Malmbjerg.
regions.price: Modeled 2030-reference LCOE: 297 EUR/MWh for diesel business-as-usual; 199 EUR/MWh for the lowest-cost South solar-wind-diesel mix; 60 EUR/MWh for upgraded hydropower with a roughly 100 km line

regions.nuclear_position: The February 2026 government-commissioned mine-energy study does not evaluate nuclear or microreactors; it compares diesel, solar, wind, batteries, hydropower, tidal energy, and e-fuels.
regions.microreactor_activity: No microreactor procurement, study, MOU, or tariff filing was found in the government mine-energy report or in the named mines' power documents reviewed.
blockers: A 1-20 MW reactor must beat the study's 199-297 EUR/MWh delivered-power band while financing construction before mine revenue begins
The study assumes a 20-year mine life, shorter than many nuclear asset lives, creating residual-value and early-closure risk
The modeled 100% solar-wind South case reaches 2,761 EUR/MWh because it requires 893 MW wind, 50 MW solar, and 351 MWh of batteries
Some mine demand data were unavailable or confidential, so 10 MW generalized loads replace project-specific profiles
regions.microreactor_read: The report creates a direct pricing screen for a 10 MW-class firm source: below 199 EUR/MWh beats the modeled least-cost hybrid, while 297 EUR/MWh is the diesel ceiling. A viable offer also needs a 20-year commercial structure and clear residual-value treatment.
